record.original_question: Let (K_i)_{i\ge 1} be compact subsets of ℂ with 0\in K_i for every i and \operatorname{diam}(K_i)	o 0, and define S={∑_{j=1}^∞ x_j\mid x_j\in K_j} with tails R_z. Under what conditions on K_i and R_z does S have fractal structure, and what is the Hausdorff dimension of S in those cases?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each $i\geq 1$ let $K_i\subset\mathbb{C}$ be a non-empty compact set with $0\in K_i$, and assume $\operatorname{diam}(K_i)\to 0$ as $i\to\infty$ (so that every choice $x_j\in K_j$ produces an absolutely-bounded series). Define the set of subsums
$$S \;=\; \Big\{\sum_{j=1}^{\infty} x_j \;:\; x_j\in K_j \text{ for every } j\geq 1\Big\}\subset\mathbb{C},$$
and for each $z\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ let the $z$-th tail set be
$$R_z \;=\; \Big\{\sum_{j=z+1}^{\infty} x_j \;:\; x_j\in K_j\Big\}.$$

Determine necessary and/or sufficient conditions on the sequence $(K_i)_{i\geq 1}$ and on the tail sets $(R_z)_{z\geq 0}$ under which the set $S$ exhibits a fractal structure (e.g. is self-similar, of non-integer Hausdorff dimension, has empty interior together with positive lower dimension, or is a Cantor-type / Cantorval-type set in $\mathbb{C}$). In each such case, compute or give explicit formulas/bounds for the Hausdorff dimension $\dim_H(S)$ in terms of the geometric data of $(K_i)$ and $(R_z)$.
artifact.category_tag: Subsums of null sequences and fractal geometry
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a survey on subsums of null sequences. Related work on real-line achievement sets and Cantorvals (e.g. Guthrie–Nymann-type series) addresses fractal/Hausdorff-dimension questions in special cases, but no general characterization or dimension formula for complex-valued subsum sets $S=\{\sum x_j:x_j\in K_j\}$ (with $K_j\subset\mathbb{C}$, $\operatorname{diam}(K_j)\to0$) appears in the literature. The general problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Fractal analysis of Guthrie-Nymann's set and its generalisations
status_evidence.snippet: Hausdorff dimension of the boundary of Cantorvals that arise as attractors of IFS or as sets of subsums of numerical series is a question that deserves special attention. NSS-sets differ from self-similar sets because they consist of countably many self-copies, so it is not easy to calculate their Hausdorff dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work treats only special real-line cases and notes that the dimension of subsum sets is hard to compute, with the general (and complex-valued) case not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Subsums of Null Sequences: A Survey and Open Questions
status_evidence.snippet: Survey collecting open questions on the structure of sets of subsums S of null sequences, including questions on fractal structure and Hausdorff dimension in the complex setting.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed among open questions in a survey.
